source.title: Stationary Markovian Arrival Processes, Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: For an irreducible Markov Modulated Poisson Process (MMPP), modeled as a Markovian Arrival Process with a finite irreducible continuous-time Markov chain phase process X(t), generator Q = C + D, diagonal event matrix D = diag(lambda_i) with lambda_i >= 0, and C = Q - D, let T_1^alpha be the first inter-event time in the event-stationary version of the process. Let c^2 = Var(T_1^alpha) / E[T_1^alpha]^2 be the squared coefficient of variation of that event-stationary inter-event time. Is c^2 >= 1 for every irreducible MMPP?
accepted.context_brief: SCV lower bound for irreducible MMPPs

evidence.quote: A common way to parameterize MAPs is by considering the generator, Q, of an irreducible finite state CTMC and setting Q = C + D. Roughly speaking, the matrix C determines state transitions without event counts and the matrix D determines event counts.
MMPP: A MAP with a diagonal matrix D is an MMPP. MMPPs correspond to doubly-stochastic Poisson processes (also known as Cox processes) where the modulating process is driven by a CTMC.

Consider the squared coefficient of variation and the limiting index of dispersion of counts given by, c2 = Var(T alpha 1 ) E2[T alpha 1 ] , and d2 = lim t->infinity Var(N(t)) E[N(t)] , (1) where T alpha 1 is the time of the first event, taken from the event stationary version.
Conjecture 4.1. For an irreducible MMPP, c2 >= 1.

accepted.question_text: For an irreducible Markov Modulated Poisson Process (MMPP), modeled as a Markovian Arrival Process with generator Q = C + D and diagonal event matrix D, let pi be the stationary distribution of the background continuous-time Markov chain and alpha be the stationary distribution of the embedded event chain. Let T_1^pi denote the first-event time when the MAP is initialized in the time-stationary distribution pi, and let T_1^alpha denote the first-event time when it is initialized in the event-stationary distribution alpha. Does the stochastic order T_1^pi >=_st T_1^alpha hold for every irreducible MMPP?
accepted.context_brief: Stochastic order for MMPP first-event times

evidence.quote: Since Q is assumed irreducible and finite, it has a unique stationary distribution pi satisfying piQ = 0', pi1 = 1.
Of further interest is the embedded discrete-time Markov chain with irreducible stochastic matrix P = (-C)-1D and stationary distribution alpha, where alphaP = alpha and alpha1 = 1.
Further, if eta = pi then the MAP is time-stationary and if eta = alpha it is event stationary, where pi and alpha are associated stationary distributions.
Conjecture 4.2. For an irreducible MMPP, T pi 1 >=st T alpha 1.

accepted.question_text: For a Markov Modulated Poisson Process (MMPP), modeled as a Markovian Arrival Process with diagonal event matrix D and event-stationary first inter-event time T_1^alpha, let c^2 = Var(T_1^alpha) / E[T_1^alpha]^2 be the squared coefficient of variation. If c^2 = 1, must the MMPP be a Poisson process?

evidence.quote: MMPP: A MAP with a diagonal matrix D is an MMPP. MMPPs correspond to doubly-stochastic Poisson processes (also known as Cox processes) where the modulating process is driven by a CTMC.

Consider the squared coefficient of variation and the limiting index of dispersion of counts given by, c2 = Var(T alpha 1 ) E2[T alpha 1 ] , and d2 = lim t->infinity Var(N(t)) E[N(t)] , (1) where T alpha 1 is the time of the first event, taken from the event stationary version.
But, we believe that all MMPPs with c2 = 1 are Poisson. Yet, we don't have a proof.

accepted.question_text: For a Markov Modulated Poisson Process (MMPP) with diagonal event matrix D = diag(lambda_1, ..., lambda_p), where lambda_i is the Poisson event rate associated with phase i, let c^2 be the squared coefficient of variation of the event-stationary first inter-event time. If c^2 = 1, must all phase-dependent rates lambda_i be equal?
accepted.context_brief: Equality of MMPP phase rates when c^2 = 1

evidence.quote: The parameters of an MMPPp are D = diag(lambda_i), where lambda_i >= 0 for i = 1, . . . , p, and C = Q - D.
Further, we believe that for an MMPP, if c2 = 1 then all lambda_i are equal (the converse is trivially true). We don't have a proof of this either.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Versions of Conjectures 1 and 2 also hold for Cox processes under suitable regularity conditions.

evidence.quote: In fact, since any Cox process can be approximated by an MMPP, we believe that versions of conjectures 1 and 2 also hold for Cox processes under suitable regularity conditions.
